title: The Crow
notes: That Qabil carried his brother's body for a time, not knowing what to do, comes from classical commentary.
imagePrompt: A barren, cracked field at dusk, the sky a bruised purple fading to a thin line of orange on the horizon, a single leafless tree in silhouette; a dim grey figure of light hunched on the ground beside a shape covered in shadow; a black crow drawn in crisp, detailed ink strokes, standing out sharply from the soft painting, digging at the earth with beak and claws, small bursts of dirt flying; at the end, a small mound of earth beside the kneeling figure as the crow flies toward the fading sunset.

beats.say: At dusk, Qabil sat beside his brother's body, lost, not knowing what to do.
A crow glided down and landed a few steps away.

verse.en: Then Allah sent a crow searching in the ground to show him how to hide the disgrace of his brother.

beats.say: It scratched at the earth, dug a small hollow, and pushed the soil back over it.

verse.en: O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the body of my brother?
And he became of the regretful.
